title: Interview with Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo
author: Modern
content:
Der Spiegel
 
42
/1996 (Oct. 14, 1996), p. 165

Translation (
see below
).

East Timor

,,They keep us like slaves''

Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, 48, was awarded the Peace Nobel Prize last week -- together with coordinator abroad of the East-Timorese resistence movement, José Ramos-Horta, 51. Bishop Belo is head of the Catholic church of East Timor since 1983.

SPIEGEL:
 Monsignore Belo, the former Portuguese colony of East Timor was overrun by the Indonesian army in 1975. since then, Jakarta has kept your country occupied, in the opinion of the UN in contradiction to international law. How does this tell on the people of the island?

Belo:
 The Indonesian soldiery, which has robbed us of our freedom and
destroyed our culture, treats us as scabby dogs. Justice is alien to them. The Indonesians keep us like slaves.

SPIEGEL:
 That sounds harsh for a man of the church. Have you already
tried it with dialogue?

Belo:
 These people are not accessible for arguments. If we talk, they beat us. Every day people come to me, who have been tortured. The most hideous things are happening. Nine times there has been attempts to kill me.

SPIEGEL:
 the speaker in exile of the resistence movement. Ramos-Horta, claims that, after the occupation of the island 21 years ago, approximately 200,000 of the originally 650,00 East Timorese got killed. Jakarta speaks of some ten thousand dead. What is true?

Belo:
 At that time I was abroad for studies. I only know one thing: in my church register there had been 650,000 listed before the occupation. five years later there were but 300,000 left. Churchgoers tell me of the cruelest massacres. and don't forget that even in 1991 the Indonesians carried out a massacre in the Santa Cruz cemetry in Dili, on which occasion several hundred people disappeared.

SPIEGEL:
 Can trust between the Indonesian state power and the East Timorese be restored?

Belo:
 After all that has happenned, hardly. The main source of trouble is the military, it enjoys privileges which leads to monstrous misuse of power. The people here want to be independent and to live in a state of their own, no matter how poor they would then be.
